question: Does the signed input and target actually consumed by DNb05 preserve odor-relevant polarity, and is the 20-ms native trajectory numerically concordant with the reference engine?

rivals.A: The 629 left PN general-destination substitution generates an asymmetric downstream drive; its prospective flag intervention is distinct and remains pending.
rivals.B: Central convergence and thresholds route useful contrast to DNb05 while suppressing the sampled DNa02 pair; measure both pairs in the actual native rate kernels before selecting any circuit lesion.
rivals.C: Baseline motor command and decoder produce the sham yaw independent of body asymmetry; 400-ms body-only open-loop result in campaign 11 supports the command component, but the neural/decoder source remains unknown.

prototype: B diagnostic only: extend the existing native CUDA FP64 sideband with DNb05 R10065/L10118, no change to biological equations or output; one-ms sham observer on/off exact state, then 20-ms sham native/reference comparison including hidden state, discrete events, DNb05 and DNa02 target.
falsifiers: A sideband target reconstruction error >1e-9, one-ms scientific on/off difference, nonfinite, or 20-ms comparison mismatch above frozen 1e-4 blocks numerical certification. Observed DNb05 contrast at sham alone cannot establish odor steering.
limits: No biological parameter adjustment, decoder retuning, 400-ms extrapolation, stage-3 admission, or replacement of anatomical edges. Instrumentation may store six selected rows but must not read debug data in model equations.
stop: Stop after any source-identity, ownership, observer-equivalence or domain failure and preserve the failed run. A mismatched reference result is a diagnostic failure, not a reason to loosen tolerance.
